blocks.text: The newest complete Ubuntu session confirms full as the exact optimized default: median runtime falls from 791.2145 to 452.69625 ms per 100 x 100 frame, a 42.78% reduction (1.7478x). The earlier shadow-only change achieved 22.63%. Relative to its historical 611.02 ms optimized median, full is about 25.91% faster; that comparison is across separate sessions, not a direct randomized ablation.

blocks.text: The benchmark renders a deterministic scene with seven spheres, a halfspace, two point lights, materials, shadows and recursive reflected rays. For each pixel it creates a primary ray, finds intersections, selects the closest valid hit and computes shading/reflections. The exact upstream behavior, including its geometric and checkerboard quirks, is the reference; correcting that behavior would change the benchmark.

Vector, Point, Ray, Sphere, Halfspace and scene/material objects form a graph of ordinary Python objects. Coordinates are boxed Python floats accessed through attributes; object lists drive intersection loops. Canvas stores byte colour data with array. Dependencies are Python math/array and pyperf for the official harness. There is no NumPy or native numeric kernel in the final software.

The baseline wrapper invokes upstream.bench_raytrace itself, including its scene setup and render loop. Image-file writing is outside the upstream timer and is enabled only for checks. The optimized variant installs selected methods temporarily and restores them afterward. The original source and baseline wrappers were not changed during this work.

Newest matched pair: results/raytrace_baseline_20260920-074314_1800 and results/raytrace_optimized_20260920-075734_1800. Comparison: results/session_all_20260920-074308_674/comparison_raytrace. Session explicitly selects full; all captured source hashes match the reviewed files.

pages.title: Measure the workload before changing it

blocks.text: The target is Ubuntu 22.04.5, Linux 5.15.0-1106-kvm, one virtual CPU exposing an Intel Xeon E5-2630 v3 at 2.40 GHz. Clean timing uses release CPython 3.10.12, CPU 0 affinity, a fixed hash seed and cyclic GC disabled. The VM governor is unavailable; host scheduling, frequency and contention are not fully controlled. These are measurements of this guest, not bare-metal Haswell limits.

blocks.text: The custom wrapper calls the actual upstream bench function and uses its timer. A minimal pyperf import stub exposes time.perf_counter; it does not implement pyperf.Runner. Thus this is an upstream-workload experiment through a custom harness, alongside a separate official pyperformance baseline run. That distinction does not invalidate the experiment; the workload, timer boundaries and comparison controls must be explicit.

Runtime reduction = 100 x (1 - optimized median / baseline median). Speedup = baseline median / optimized median. We use runtime reduction for the declared 7% target. CV = sample standard deviation / mean. Samples from separate TXT and CSV perf invocations are not pooled.

Latest session saves a four-frame exact optimized gate covering both reference and candidate. Standalone baseline verification is smaller despite its phase label; the saved optimized gate provides the actual batch comparison. Some perf phases remain labelled requested although their artifacts exist. py-spy is explicitly disabled; official pyperformance applies only to the baseline.

pages.title: Initial hypothesis and historical shadow evidence

blocks.text: A flame graph is an aggregation of sampled call stacks, not a timeline. Width is inclusive sampled weight; height is stack depth, not elapsed time. Self weight counts only samples whose leaf is that symbol. Children weight includes descendants and overlaps other ancestors. The libc start routine can therefore have a huge inclusive share while doing little direct work. Aggregate a function across every folded stack: the top-30 listing is incomplete, and repeated appearances must not be mistaken for separate causes.

The repeating evaluator/vectorcall chain reflects nested Python method execution. Tall similar stacks alone cannot count calls or price each call. cProfile supplies the stronger mechanism: one frame has 509,873 dot calls, 277,865 Point.__sub__/isPoint calls and 179,457 sphere intersection calls. In total it records 3,092,298 calls, including non-Python calls. A fixed claim of 1,600 machine instructions for every call is not supported.

blocks.caption: Equal work: one frame per native debug profile, period 5 million cycles. These selected rows are self counts. Total samples: 1,073 baseline and 823 shadow-ray. Counts are indicative; sparse differences are not precise estimates.

blocks.text: The actionable question is whether identical geometry is repeatedly wrapped in new objects. In lightIsVisible, the same origin and light direction are used while testing successive objects. Reconstructing and normalizing that ray for every object repeats work without changing the ray. Reusing it once per visibility query predicts fewer Ray/Vector creations, normalizations, dot products and guard calls, while leaving the number of intersection queries unchanged.

CPython is a bytecode interpreter, not an AST interpreter. _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault includes bytecode execution, operand handling, loop control and reference work; its self share is not pure call overhead. Debug checks and different code generation change costs. High IPC and few cache misses support an instruction-work hypothesis but do not identify a precise hardware stall limit. Reject negative top-down fractions and unsupported PMU events rather than interpreting them as valid measurements or zeros.

pages.title: Shadow reuse: the measured first change

blocks.text: shadow_ray builds one ray per visibility query and reuses it for each object test. This requires read-only intersection methods; custom or mutating implementations use the original path. It retains object traversal order, short-circuit behavior, comparison thresholds and upstream handling of intersections beyond the light. It does not introduce a different visibility rule.

rows: 144,344 fewer objects; import overhead in both.
25.65% fewer calls; not a runtime fraction.

blocks.text: This combination is stronger evidence than a large interpreter percentage: a concrete source change removes a known repeated computation; exact call counts change by the predicted amount; equal-work instructions and clean runtime both fall. It supports redundant Python work as an important cost, without claiming a single universal bottleneck.

Pixel identity was checked at 24 x 24, 100 x 100 and 37 x 23. The 100 x 100 PPM SHA-256 prefix is 11f2c36b02044f11. Current verification checks every frame in the requested batch, independent sizes, and baseline restoration. A matching image alone is supplemented by raw colour, geometry and randomized tests for the new full kernel.

Historical shadow artifacts do not fully capture the optimized source hash, and manifests record a dirty working tree. The workload records and saved tests support the result, but do not reconstruct every historical local edit. Current workflows capture source hashes and explicit session paths.

blocks.text: These local results use CPython 3.14.6 on arm64 macOS, 11 rotating repetitions and two 100 x 100 frames per sample. They are exploratory, not Ubuntu measurements; small individual regressions are not resolved reliably. Effects are not additive, and a faster combination does not prove every component helps. Keep explicit kernels for target-VM ablation.

Strict correctness means bit-identical benchmark pixels and preserved tested computation at successful boundaries. Tests include raw float bits for 1,000 randomized sphere cases and edge cases, camera components, prequantization colours, varied scenes, custom fallbacks, ties and restoration. All four production-sized frames match in the saved full-batch gate. Twenty-four raytrace tests passed; all 63 combined software tests passed.

Rejected or deferred: unconditional guard deletion breaks polymorphism; exact-class rejection without fallback narrows behavior; fixing upstream shadow/checkerboard semantics changes the task. Lower precision, approximate roots, a new integrator or answer caching violate the exact reference contract. Compiled native backends remain a possible separate experiment, outside the agreed pure-Python implementation.

Retention decision after the new Ubuntu run: keep full as a tested bundle. The additional work reductions occur in the predicted functions and the whole bundle is much faster. No new VM isolated or leave-one-out ablation was collected, so this does not prove every component contributes positive runtime savings. In particular, guards and checkerboard were slightly slower alone in the old Mac experiment. Keep those controls and optional slots available; do not claim their individual VM gains.

blocks.caption: Eleven independent processes per arm, four frames per process. Dashed lines are medians. Every observation is retained; arms were collected in separate blocks.

blocks.text: Runtime, instructions, cycles and calls move together, as predicted by removal of repeated setup. A separate perf CSV batch also shows about 23% fewer instructions; do not merge it with TXT samples. L1 misses decrease 13.38%, yet their rate rises from 2.65% to 2.98% because loads fall faster. A worse rate does not mean more misses or a slower program.

All optimized timing observations beat all baseline observations. The effect is much larger than within-block variation, although VM drift remains unmeasured. The official pyperformance baseline reports about 800 +/- 5 ms, consistent with the custom baseline. It is a cross-check, not an official optimized result.

pages.title: Newest full run: a further substantial improvement

blocks.caption: Eleven independent processes per arm, four frames per process; all observations retained. Dashed lines mark medians. Arms were collected in separate blocks.

blocks.text: Median runtime reduction is 42.7846%, saving 338.51825 ms/frame. Even the slowest optimized process beats the fastest baseline by 41.13%. Dispersion is small relative to the effect, but sequential collection leaves slow VM drift unmeasured. The generated 2x-noise rule is a heuristic, not a significance test.

The earlier shadow-only baseline was 789.7555 ms, only 0.185% below this baseline; its optimized median was 611.02275 ms. Full is 25.91% below that older optimized median. This is corroborating historical evidence, not an isolated estimate of the added components because the experiments were collected at different times.

Official baseline cross-check: 20 value-producing workers, 60 values; median about 801 ms, mean 801 +/- 5 ms. It uses a different harness and does not supply an official optimized result. Full source SHA: 5badaf27f0f9519fd0d2779bd37c745feadcf76e31fbde833cd89dfbb5770d55.

pages.title: What changed: fewer calls, objects and instructions

blocks.text: * Shadow column is the historical shadow-only profile. The deterministic query counts match across scenes; this is a work comparison, not a same-session runtime ablation. New full total process calls: 3,092,309 -> 881,684 (-71.49%), including interpreter/library calls.

All 179,457 sphere tests remain. Vector constructions fall by 347,458: shadow reuse removes 144,344; scalar spheres 179,457; camera reuse 19,800; checkerboard 3,857. These sum exactly to the observed delta. Scalar spheres also remove two dot helpers per test. Direct hit selection removes the intersection list/helper. Exact images and unchanged primitive, visibility and pixel counts support preserved work; these counts do not isolate each change's runtime contribution.

A separate five-run CSV counter batch corroborates the TXT result: instructions -43.87%, cycles -42.41%, L1 loads -43.75%. Both batches show about 43% fewer L1 load misses. IPC decreases modestly (TXT 2.658 -> 2.574); fewer instructions explain the speedup. These are separate counting experiments and include process startup outside the clean timer.

blocks.text: The interpreter and renderer remain on the stack, and both SVGs fill their canvas width. The remaining evaluator share can grow while its absolute samples fall. The normalized differential graph shows redistribution, not saved seconds; wrapper ancestry also changes. Unknown frames occur somewhere in 240 baseline and 88 optimized sample paths, so exact attribution remains incomplete.

The remaining largest traced Python function is scalar sphere: 0.29546 s self and 0.29646 s cumulative across 179,457 calls. Its self time increased after work was inlined, while inclusive sphere time fell from about 0.78140 s. That is attribution moving into the function, not a regression. ray_colour, visibility, shading and remaining vector helpers follow. Tracing times are not release fractions or hardware speedup ceilings.

L1 miss rate rises slightly (2.966% -> 3.031%) despite fewer misses. Generic cache-miss counts disagree across TXT/CSV; cache-sampling runs have only 12 and 3 samples. Reject cache hotspot claims from them. Negative top-down fractions are invalid; LLC events are unsupported. Kernel/BPF warnings qualify symbol interpretation; reported lost samples are zero.
The proposal offloads a complete ray-sphere intersection rather than individual floating-point instructions. This boundary can remove Python objects, calls and dispatch as well as execute arithmetic.

hardware/rtl/ray_sphere_accel.sv contains the sequential controller, operand/result registers, status and ready/valid protocol. The datapath uses actual unmodified BSD-licensed Berkeley HardFloat Release 1 RTL: one shared add/sub unit, one multiplier and an iterative square-root unit. There are no real-number or software-math placeholders in the synthesizable datapath.

cp = center - origin
v = (cp.x*dx + cp.y*dy) + cp.z*dz
q = (cp.x*cp.x + cp.y*cp.y) + cp.z*cp.z
disc = r*r - (q - v*v)
result = no_root if disc < 0 else v - sqrt(disc)

Each operation rounds separately to binary64, nearest-even, including gradual underflow. There is no FMA, reassociation, FP32 or approximate reciprocal root. A tangent and a negative returned distance preserve upstream behavior; software applies its original hit-selection rule. Finite inputs/intermediates, nonnegative radius and caller-normalized direction define the supported domain. Invalid/nonfinite cases return an error for CPU fallback.

HardFloat source and license: hardware/vendor/ provenance and license files. Primary specification: https://www.jhauser.us/arithmetic/HardFloat-1/doc/HardFloat-Verilog.html. Detailed ports, schedule and host format: docs/HARDWARE_DESIGN.md and hardware/.

Design reassessment: sphere intersections remain frequent, but square root is reached only 6,934 times (3.864% of 179,457 queries). The current core is a single-query sequential function with no resident scene or internal batch controller. A batched geometric core or a small reusable FP64 command engine are alternatives, not implemented replacements. More general hardware is not automatically faster; operand residency and the software offload boundary need justification.

Resource sharing limits replication and potential switching but also throughput. FP64 rounding/sqrt remain substantial logic; no numerical area, power or achieved frequency is claimed. A pipelined or multi-lane version trades area/control/clocking for throughput. An equivalent native CPU batch is necessary to separate escaping Python from hardware value.

pages.title: New workload evidence changes the estimate

rows: 640 operand bits + 32-bit tag; distance/status/flags response; one outstanding query; ready/valid and held response.
Separate FP64 rounding, ordered expressions, caller-normalized rays; finite supported domain with CPU fallback on error.
Arithmetic/control RTL and host packing exist. Renderer batching, transport/DMA and driver remain proposed.
50 MHz target assumption; 20 cycles/miss, 80/root budget. No achieved timing or HDL simulation.

blocks.text: The full-profile math.sqrt caller map records 6,934 sphere calls; 37,715 other square roots belong to magnitude and one to import setup. Thus h = 6,934 / 179,457 = 0.0386388. Source control flow confirms that sphere calls sqrt only after a nonnegative discriminant. This measured workload mix replaces the earlier all-root assumption; it is not a measured hardware speed.

With the same assumed 50 MHz, 1 GB/s aggregate payload bandwidth, batch size 1,024, 10 us launch/batch and 100 ns native packing/query, modeled core time is 80.1036 ms. Transfer is 18.6635 ms, launch 1.7600 ms and packing 17.9457 ms: 118.4728 ms total offload cost. Against the new full software time of 452.69625 ms, break-even requires removing more than 26.17% of release runtime.

T_new = T_full x (1 - f) + T_offload. f remains unknown: cProfile sphere share cannot supply it. The modeled 7% runtime reduction would require f > 33.17%; this is a sensitivity point, not a separate mandated hardware target. Batching can change early-exit queries and h, so the original query mix must be rechecked after integration.

The old all-root case against shadow-only software remains historical evidence, not the current default estimate. If applied to faster full software, that all-root stress case needs 71.90% removable time just to break even. No hardware improvement occurred between estimates; only software baseline and workload assumptions changed.

pages.title: What is established and what comes next

blocks.text: Full is now the selected exact raytrace implementation, with a 42.78% target-VM runtime reduction and a saved four-frame correctness gate. The earlier 22.63% shadow result remains the first measured step. Additional scalarization, call removal and direct traversal visibly remove work; the aggregate result does not establish the isolated value of every component.

Keep all diagnostic kernels, including optional slots, for controlled comparisons. New individual VM ablations are needed before ranking or pruning small changes. Hardware remains a candidate: the measured low root fraction improves the analytical estimate, while faster software tightens the budget. The next hardware decision should compare a batched geometric core with a small reusable arithmetic engine and account for native CPU execution.
